senses.definition: (heading) A pile.

subsenses.definition: A large pile of hay, grain, straw, or the like, larger at the bottom than the top, sometimes covered with thatch.

senses.definition: (heading) In computing.

subsenses.definition: (programming) A linear data structure in which items inserted are removed in reverse order (the last item inserted is the first one to be removed).
(computing, often with "the") A stack data structure stored in main memory that is manipulated during machine language procedure call related instructions.

quotes.text: When the microprocessor decodes the JSR opcode, it stores the operand into the TEMP register and pushes the current contents of the PC ($00 0128) onto the stack.
quotes.reference: 1992, Michael A. Miller, The 68000 Microprocessor Family: Architecture, Programming, and Applications, page 47:

subsenses.definition: (networking) An implementation of a protocol suite (set of protocols forming a layered architecture).
examples: A TCP/IP stack is a library or set of libraries or of OS drivers that take care of networking.

subsenses.definition: A combination of interdependent, yet individually replaceable, software components or technologies used together on a system.

quotes.text: A Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP (LAMP) stack is a configuration of four popular products for hosting websites.
quotes.reference: 2016, John Paul Mueller, AWS For Admins For Dummies, John Wiley & Sons, →ISBN, page 323:

senses.definition: (mathematics) A generalization of schemes in algebraic geometry and of sheaves.
(geology) A coastal landform, consisting of a large vertical column of rock in the sea.

quotes.text: A boat's-crew landed one time upon one of the stacks with the intention of attacking the seals.

senses.definition: (figuratively) A large amount of an object.
examples: They paid him a stack of money to keep quiet.

senses.definition: (military) A pile of rifles or muskets in a cone shape.
(poker) The amount of money a player has on the table.
(heading) In architecture.

subsenses.definition: A number of flues embodied in one structure, rising above the roof.

senses.definition: (Australia, slang) A fall or crash, a prang.

(video games) The quantity of a given item which fills up an inventory slot or bag.

senses.definition: (transitive) To arrange in a stack, or to add to an existing stack.
examples: Please stack those chairs in the corner.

senses.definition: (transitive, card games) To arrange the cards in a deck in a particular manner, especially for cheating.
examples: This is the third hand in a row where you've drawn four of a kind. Someone is stacking the deck!

senses.definition: (transitive, by extension) To arrange or fix to obtain an advantage; to deliberately distort the composition of (an assembly, committee, etc.).
examples: The Government was accused of stacking the parliamentary committee.

senses.definition: (transitive, poker) To take all the money another player currently has on the table.
examples: I won Jill's last $100 this hand; I stacked her!

senses.definition: (transitive, US, Australia, slang) To crash; to fall.
examples: Jim couldn't make it today as he stacked his car on the weekend.
